items.title: 68429_Walter P. Thomas oral history interview
items.q: Mitchell Parrish was a lyrics writer, and he wrote the lyrics to 'Minnie the Moocher.'

ctx.x: "Hi-Di-Ho" was a public domain song named "Willie The Weeper." And Mills got Parrish to write the words to "Minnie The Moocher"... He took the same lyrics and the same melody, and made it "Minnie The Moocher." That's a story within itself. So we got this arrangement... I wish I could think of that guy's name. He finally went down to Brazil. He was a good arranger, but he didn't fit what needed -- for "Minnie The Moocher" anyway. So we kept fooling with this arrangement, going over it and over it and over it. But…

So we played at the Cotton Club. So Cab said, the night we closed at the Cotton Club to do the recording the next day... He said, "Foots..." He just said, "Do something on 'Minnie The Moocher.'" And that's all he said. So I went home that night, and got up early the next morning, and went to my piano -- and the melody just came to me." And I'll really confess, I copied the tune, the melody a little from "Get Happy." You know, "Get Happy" goes... [SINGS
